accuracy.evidence: Arctic as the Arctic Ocean, mostly covered by floating sea ice a few metres thick, ringed by North America, Greenland, Europe and Asia (NSIDC 'All About Sea Ice', National Geographic Education 'Arctic'); Antarctica as the fifth-largest continent, bedrock under an ice sheet about 2 km thick on average, surrounded by the Southern Ocean (NSIDC 'Quick facts on ice sheets', British Antarctic Survey); Antarctica colder than the Arctic with the −89.2 °C Vostok record (WMO weather and climate extremes archive); about four million Arctic residents (Arctic Council) and no permanent Antarctic population, only research stations (Antarctic Treaty Secretariat / COMNAP); polar bears hunt seals from sea ice, wild penguins live only in the Southern Hemisphere (WWF, British Antarctic Survey). Kid text keeps these as 'a frozen ocean' / 'a huge piece of land' without wrong simplification.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-years confusions about the poles: the two poles are the same kind of place (m6, tag middle, map step), there is land under the North Pole (drill prediction, p1, tag under), people live in towns in Antarctica (build prediction, house/school/shop refused in Antarctica, p5, tag people), and the cartoon polar-bear-with-penguins picture (poster prediction, m2, tags bear and bird). Also 'the Arctic is colder' (sort card 'the colder one', m3, tag cold).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagarcant is built on this topic's own contrast: two cross-sections where a drill is dragged down until it hits sea water under thin ice (north) or rock under a thick ice sheet (south), two top-down maps whose middle must be filled with ocean or land, a town builder that refuses homes in Antarctica, and two posters with an intruder to move across. flagglobe (finding the poles, Equator, Sun angle) and flagpolaran (blubber, huddle, seasonal coat) use none of these; the lab_distinct gate passed under 30% against every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each contrast before the text states it: the drill visibly breaks into water in one panel and stops on rock in the other; dropping 'land' in the Arctic middle is refused with a pointer back to the drill; a house dropped on Antarctica is refused because nobody lives there all year; tapping the walrus or whale says it belongs and to look for the animal from the other end of the Earth. The sort step then makes them apply all of it.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with a tempting wrong option, each tested by the next task: 'land, like rock' under the North Pole (the drill hits water), 'a frozen ocean' in the middle of the Antarctic (the map shows land), 'yes, in towns' for families in Antarctica (homes are refused), and 'yes, they live together on the ice' for polar bears and penguins (the posters are wrong). The reveal line names the right answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions (under the North Pole ice, what Antarctica is, where penguins live, where polar bears live, where towns are, which is colder, what surrounds the Arctic Ocean). Wrong options carry tags under, middle, where, bird, bear, people and cold, each with its own message naming the slip, e.g. 'Nobody lives in Antarctica all year. People live in Arctic towns; Antarctica only has science stations.'

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes (kid and adult within the Flesch–Kincaid limits; the first adult draft read at grade 10.7 and was rewritten into shorter sentences). Kid paragraphs use short concrete sentences ('Under the ice at the South Pole there is rock.') and introduce one new word, continent, with its meaning. Young-mode buttons are 56 px tall with 1.15 rem text.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: where each pole is, ocean vs land, who lives there, animals and which is colder. Adult: curriculum link and key words, the geography with numbers, named mistakes with the correct facts, then exactly what the lab does. No filler pattern matched and the 12% duplicate gate passed against 645 Polar Animals and the Where Are the Poles? lesson.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 light and 360 px Android light and dark screenshots after Show me on every step. Fixed from the first pass: the 'land all round / ocean all round' labels sat across the thin map ring at 11 px, now they sit under each map at 13 px; building, poster and clue labels raised to 13 px. The two panels, drill rods, tokens and cards fit above the message strip at 360 px; real pointer drags of the drill, ocean/land tokens and poster animals were tested at 390 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin: 'Drill at the North/South Pole', '<pole> middle: ocean/land', one button per pole for the current building and clue card, and one button per poster animal. The canvas aria-label and live region carry every message. walk.cjs passed axe WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console or page errors.
